articles.title: Amorim’s Milan live up to billing as teenage star Cissè upstages signings | Nicky Bandini
articles.summary: Rossoneri overcome fascinating first challenge at Torino as teams across Serie A give homegrown talent a chance. “I love Cissè. I love Cissè.” Ruben Amorim had not yet taken charge of his first competitive game as Milan manager but already he was furnishing journalists with soundbites and…
body: Alphadjo Cissè is a 19-year-old attacking midfielder who signed for Milan from Verona in February but only joined up with them this summer, after completing the season-long loan he had already begun at Catanzaro in Serie B. He scored six goals in 22 games there, missing the second half of the campaign with a thigh injury. Previously he had played a combined 14 minutes for Verona across three substitute appearances in the top flight.

Yet Amorim spoke of Cissè like a man who knew something that the rest of the world doesn’t. More than his words, it was the body language: hands rubbing together in anticipation, lip curled at one corner into an emoji-like version of a smirk.

Cissè would start away to Torino the following evening. Within 75 seconds of kick-off, he had taken the first shot of the game: racing forward to hook a Ruben Loftus-Cheek cross into the side netting from an acute angle beyond the far post.

articles.title: Mercedes’ Wolff wary that Norris and Hamilton are genuine F1 title contenders
articles.summary: Mercedes team principal: ‘It could become tighter’ Title leader Antonelli will take grid penalties in Monza. McLaren’s Lando Norris and Ferrari’s Lewis Hamilton are genuine contenders for the Formula One world championship, according to the Mercedes team principal, Toto Wolff, who watched Norris…
body: With Mercedes’ early-season dominance looking to have been all but erased, Wolff noted that there would be no quick fix for the team who could not develop at the same rate as their rivals because they had opted to use their budget differently.

Norris won the race at Zandvoort for McLaren with the team having brought several car upgrades to the meeting, beating the Mercedes’ of title leader Kimi Antonelli and George Russell into second and third. Ferrari have also moved closer to Mercedes, who won eight of the opening 12 meetings, including all of the first six.

Antonelli leads Hamilton, who was fourth in Zandvoort, and Russell by 59 points in the championship and Norris by 83. However, Wolff expected the fight to become tougher in the run-in to the title, with 11 races remaining.

He said he and Mercedes are “absolutely conscious of the threat. It’s not only Norris, it’s also Ferrari, even if you have a gap of 50 points to lose, that’s something you need to be worried about. This is going to be tough. It could become tighter, we need to do the optimal job every single weekend, every single session, every single weekend.”

articles.title: Boks drop Feinberg-Mngomezulu to bench for All Blacks rematch
articles.summary: Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu pays for an indifferent showing in South Africa's series opener against New Zealand, as the fly-half drops to the Springbok bench.
body: Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu has paid the price for an indifferent showing in South Africa's defeat by New Zealand, with the fly-half dropping to the bench for Saturday's rematch in Cape Town.
The All Blacks, revitalised under new coach Dave Rennie, ran out 33-16 winners in the series opener in Johannesburg.
Feinberg-Mngomezulu was turned over five times in possession and occasionally exposed in defence, before he shifted to full-back for the Springboks in the second half of Saturday's first Test.

South Africa head coach Rassie Erasmus has recalled 32-year-old double Rugby World Cup winner Handre Pollard at 10, while injuries to Cheslin Kolbe and Grant Williams have brought Ethan Hooker and Cobus Reinach into the starting line-up at wing and scrum-half respectively.

articles.title: Fans suffer firework burns and eye injuries in Eredivisie
articles.summary: Dutch side SC Cambuur says fans were left with "burns, hearing damage and eye injuries" after Feyenoord supporters threw fireworks during Sunday's Eredivisie match.
body: Dutch club SC Cambuur said fans have suffered "burns, hearing damage and eye injuries" after Feyenoord supporters threw fireworks during Sunday's league match.
Play was suspended for around 10 minutes in the first half after visiting fans in the away end at the Kooi Stadion lit a large number of red flares and threw fireworks.
Some of the fireworks were aimed towards sections containing home fans and SC Cambuur said in a statement that five supporters were confirmed to have been injured.

Feyenoord said it "firmly distances itself from the unacceptable events" and that head coach Giovanni van Bronckhorst - an assistant to Arne Slot at Liverpool last season - apologised on behalf of the club to SC Cambuur after the match.

articles.title: Arsenal star made guest of honour for former club’s derby match
articles.summary: Arsenal summer signing Christos Tzolis was the guest of honour for former side Club Brugge over the weekend, taking a ceremonial kick-off in their derby match. Photo by Alex Pantling/Getty Images.
body: Arsenal summer addition Christos Tzolis has made a strong first impression on Gunners supporters with some positive early performances, but the winger is seemingly just as popular with his former team Club Brugge.

Tzolis left Club Brugge for Arsenal in July, and it’s not unusual for fans to turn on their best players in the aftermath of transfer exits. But that’s certainly not the case here, as the 24-year-old was invited back as the guest of honour for the Bruges derby on Sunday.
Club Brugge hosted Cercle Brugge in the afternoon kick-off, and Tzolis was asked to take an honorary kick-off for the match.

Tzolis emerged from the tunnel to chants of “Tzolis! Tzolis! Tzolis!”, with the player turning to applaud the home support. He then took the ceremonial kick-off before leaving the field with a huge smile on his face, greeting former teammates as he passed them.

articles.title: Meet the Filipino tennis superstar-in-waiting with a punch to rival Pacquiao's
articles.summary: "Once it grows, it cannot be stopped" - tennis superstar-in-the-making Alex Eala is quickly becoming the biggest thing to come out of the Philippines since legendary boxer Manny Pacquiao.
body: The 21-year-old is carrying the hopes of a nation, the volume of support when she plays calling to mind the days when world boxing champion 'Pac Man' put the country on the map as a sporting force.

Few young players on the WTA Tour have experienced the level of expectation and support Eala has received ‌since she earned a place on the circuit, and she showed what all the fuss is about ‌by winning the recent Washington Open.

After a run to the fourth round of Wimbledon, which included a victory over defending champion Iga Swiatek, Eala capped her breakthrough in the US capital by rallying to defeat top seed Jessica Pegula 4-6 ​6-4 6-0 in a rain-interrupted final, becoming the first woman from her country to claim a tour-level singles crown.
Along the way, ​she beat Olympic champion Zheng Qinwen, last year's winner Leylah ‌Fernandez, second seed Elina Svitolina and four-time Grand Slam champion Naomi Osaka.
